children: U.S. stock futures climbed into green territory late on Wednesday as technology stocks rebounded after weakness at the close.
Meanwhile, a slew of economic data releases, including October’s U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) and third-quarter gross domestic product data, placated markets.
As of 9:50 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 0.44%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.58% and Nasdaq-100 futures edged 0.76% higher.

On Wednesday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Nasdaq Composite shed 147 points, closing 0.62% lower, while the S&P 500 declined 0.25%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 0.33% higher.

Technology Stocks Rebound After Selloff

U.S. stock markets closed another volatile session on Wednesday as technology stocks sold off amid declines in Nvidia (NVDA) and Anthropic (ANT) shares. However, both companies' shares recovered in the overnight session.
NVDA stock was up 1.29% at the time of writing, while ANT shares gained 1.76% to trade above its listing price.
The Kobeissi Letter noted in a post on X that retail demand for Anthropic is accelerating.

“Retail investors bought +$100 million in Anthropic, $ANT, shares on Monday, marking a 2nd consecutive daily increase in purchases.As a result, $ANT was the 2nd-most purchased stock among retail investors during that session,” it said.

The market commentator compared it to purchases on ANT’s IPO day, saying the stock attracted $60 million in inflows, making it the third-largest retail purchase on the first trading day of any IPO since 2018.
“In total, retail investors purchased +$252 million in Anthropic shares over 3 trading days ending Monday. Retail is piling into $ANT,” it said.

Stock markets have been in a frenzy over the past few weeks, amid Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and his return to the company about two weeks later. Meanwhile, Anthropic’s historic public listing briefly squeezed market liquidity.

Dan Ives, Partner and Senior Managing Director at Yorkville Ives, said in a post on X, “This growth scare worry about semis and the AI Revolution buildout is weighing heavily on tech stocks…and this will prove to be disconnected from the reality of this massive AI infrastructure path in our view.”

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump attributed the recent market selloff to the midterm election results. He said in a post on Truth Social, “Stocks are down sharply because of the November Third Election results. I wasn’t on the Ballot, but if I was, the results, just like all three times before, would have been much different, and the Stock Market, and your 401-k’s, would be BOOMING. I told you so!!!”
Data Reveals Economy Is Stronger Than Expected
On Wednesday, October’s PCE data

by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis showed that headline inflation rose to 3.8% year-over-year and increased 0.3% month-over-month, largely in line with market expectations. Core PCE climbed to 3.3% year-over-year, ahead of Street expectations of 3.2%.
Consumer personal spending increased 0.3% month-over-month, slightly below the 0.4% forecast.

Real gross domestic product increased at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis, beating market expectations of 3.5% and marking a strong upward revision from the initial advance estimate of 3.4%.
Meanwhile, the spot dollar is up to 103.714. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was trading at 4.864% at the time of writing, while the 30-year yield was at 5.254%.
Gold, Silver Bounce Back

The precious metals trade recovered following a steep slump in prices over the week. Spot gold prices rebounded above $3,500 an ounce from session lows as Treasury yields and the dollar eased off earlier gains.
At the time of writing, spot gold was trading at $3,601.52 an ounce, while spot silver recovered to $42.11 an ounce.

“For now, elevated real yields and a resilient USD remain the primary headwinds” for gold, Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, wrote in a November report, according to Bloomberg.

“A more sustained recovery will likely require clearer evidence that inflation is moderating, alongside some easing in real yields and expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening,” Wong added.
Data from the CME FedWatch tool puts the odds of a December rate hike of 25 bps at 98.1%, up from 93.5% a week ago, while the probability of a hold is up to 1.9%.
Trending Tickers To Watch
Walt Disney Co. (DIS):

The stock was in focus among retail traders on Wednesday after a Washington federal judge temporarily halted the Federal Communications Commission’s early license renewal process for eight ABC stations, noting that broadcasters cannot be punished for “disfavored speech.”
Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (VRTX):
The biotechnology company’s shares plunged nearly 7% in overnight trading after the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration
the review timeline for its experimental IgA nephropathy treatment.
Deere & Co. (DE):
The equipment manufacturer was in focus after its CEO

that the agricultural equipment downturn “troughed” in fiscal 2026 and would likely rebound in 2027, adding that North America could lead, while aging machinery in Brazil and continued data center investments offered additional growth opportunities.
Charter Communications Inc. (CHTR):
The company drew retail attention amid a second consecutive day of gains, with sentiment improving around the stock.
Other Market Trends

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) was up 0.52% in the overnight session at the time of writing, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) climbed 0.43% and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged 0.54% higher.
Oil prices edged higher, with Brent trading at $94.63 a barrel and WTI crude futures up 0.24% to $83.88 per barrel at the time of writing.
The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was down 0.26% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.
Asian markets opened higher on Thursday. South Korea's KOSPI, China’s SSE Composite index, Japan’s Nikkei 225 and Australian stocks all traded in the green at the open.

title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Edge Higher As Tech Rebounds After Selloff: DIS, VRTX, DE, CHTR In Focus
